# Generated by lodi from one machine's own package database. It says what that machine
# had installed and chose. It says nothing about who runs it or where it lives.
#
# distribution: debian (bookworm)
#
# This is a starting point, not a backup. It does not carry anything installed from
# third-party repositories, foreign and hand-built packages, snaps and flatpaks, data,
# services, users, or package versions: an apply installs a missing package at what
# the dated archive at the snapshot below offers. A third-party apt repository this machine
# installed from is written as a commented [sources] block, to take on purpose. A
# changed configuration file is captured only when lodi's scan finds no credential
# marker in it; the scan finds the shapes it knows and proves nothing more, so read
# files/ before it leaves this machine.
# The NOT CAPTURED block at the end names what this machine had that is missing from
# the declarations above it.

[host]
version = "1"
distro = "debian"
# packages = "exact": an apply makes this machine's packages what this file declares, plus
# the distribution's own base system. A package whose line you delete is removed by the next
# apply, and one a declared package still needs is kept as a dependency; each is named in the
# plan with the reason. A package installed by hand since lodi last recorded this machine is
# not removed unless the apply is given --overwrite-drift. "managed" removes only what lodi
# recorded installing.
packages = "exact"
min_lodi_version = ">=1.4.0"
# An apply installs a missing package from the dated archive at this instant, UTC;
# remove the line and it installs from the live archive instead.
snapshot = "<time>"

[packages]

# with that distribution's own base system subtracted from it.

]

# it outlives lodi.

#
#   mark_auto = ["NAME"]  an apply marks NAME automatically installed, so that
#                         removing whatever pulled it in removes NAME with it.
#   optional  = ["NAME"]  an apply that finds no such package in the index leaves
#                         NAME out and carries on, rather than stopping.
#   absent    = ["NAME"]  an apply removes NAME wherever it finds it installed.
#
# packages = "exact" under [host] is why a line taken out of this list is a package
